newsitem.title: CANADA: Avenor to shed 600 jobs, focus on core.
newsitem.headline: Avenor to shed 600 jobs, focus on core.

text.p: Avenor Inc Chief Executive Paul Gagne told reporters after the annual meeting on Tuesday that Avenor had put its failed takeover bid for Repap Enterprises Inc behind it and would shed 600 jobs to focus on its core business.
Gagne said that to improve productivity it would not wait for the price of newsprint to improve its bottom line and would focus on the Operational Excellence Forum started last year.

"We will not rely on so-called market forces to bring us back to profitability and we've announced an Operational Excellence program, which is going to improve operating earnings by C$125 million when fully implemented by the end of 1998," he said.
Gagne said that as part of its strategy, Avenor planned to reduce its 6,100-member workforce by 550 to 600 jobs, mostly through early retirement programs.
He said Avenor would not resurrect its proposal to merge with Repap after shareholders rejected the deal last month.
"The shareholders have rejected that transaction and we are not re-looking at the Repap situation," he said.
He said Avenor would also focus on finding a buyer for its 53 percent stake in Pacific Forest Products Ltd and its Gold River pulp mill.
"We're getting to be very focused...(but) Gold River will ultimately be a candidate for sale," he said.
